When do yields and equities move together?

How to interpret the four combinations

A higher discount rate reduces the present value of future profits, all else equal. A better growth outlook can raise expected profits at the same time as investors mark up the projected interest-rate path. Expected profits can also fall during a rate cut if the growth outlook deteriorates.

Jarociński and Karadi use high-frequency interest-rate and stock-price surprises to distinguish conventional policy news from news about the outlook in a structural model. Opposite directions are consistent with a conventional policy shock. Matching directions can be consistent with outlook news. These two-year government yields also reflect risk and term premia, and an announcement can convey several kinds of news. Each cell counts observed signs without identifying the cause. Yields are rounded to 0.1 basis point and equity returns to 0.01 percent before classification. A pair with a missing quote is counted as missing. Among complete pairs, a zero in either series is counted as flat.

Timing and spread definitions

The ECB workbook compares median quotes 20–10 minutes before the start with quotes 10–20 minutes after an assumed 30-minute speech. The second interval is 40–50 minutes after the start. Other news and nearby speeches can fall inside that span.

OIS changes measure repricing of overnight rates over the named tenor. They do not report the pre-speech rate level. German 2s10s subtracts the change in the two-year yield from the change in the ten-year yield. The Italy–Germany spread subtracts the change in the German ten-year yield from the change in its Italian counterpart. Positive EUR/USD means euro appreciation.

UK timing, units and coverage

The announcement window starts 10 minutes before the policy decision and ends 20 minutes after it. The 75-minute conference window starts 10 minutes before the conference and ends 5 minutes after it finishes. The researchers compare median quotes from the 10 minutes just outside each end of the window. From August 2015, the quarterly forecast was published with the decision. Earlier forecasts accompanied the conference.

Counts use the events in the workbook. It omits some releases with unavailable data, including three 7 a.m. policy announcements in 2020. Blank instrument quotes are excluded from the median. The sterling two-year swap series starts in 2009. Gilt and swap changes are in basis points. Equity and exchange-rate changes are log returns in percent. A positive GBP/USD return means sterling strengthened.

How much of the next meeting was priced before the speech?

Follow the same FOMC meeting across quotes. A contract can already imply a full quarter-point move even when it barely changes on the day a policymaker speaks.

Cook and Waller, 20 November 2026 · December fed funds futures

Cook favoured further tightening. Waller gave no rate-path guidance. The December contract rose from 95.9250 at 3 p.m. ET on Thursday to 95.9600 at 3 p.m. ET on Friday. On the same assumptions, the implied increase at the 9 December decision fell from 27.48 to 22.55 bp. The 4.93 bp decline spans both speeches and the 10 a.m. slot for two BLS releases. It leaves the size of any reaction to Cook’s speech unidentified. Cook’s remarks and earlier outlook · Waller’s remarks · BLS release schedule

Jefferson, 19 November 2026 · December fed funds futures

Before Philip Jefferson’s remarks at 9:25 a.m. ET, the last daily settlement implied 26.77 bp of tightening at the 9 December decision. The estimate had fallen 0.70 bp since Friday 13 November. By Thursday’s settlement it was back to 27.48 bp. Compare the 0.70 bp change on the speech date with the much larger amount that was already priced.

Calculation, observation times and other news

The contract settles against the calendar-month average of the effective federal funds rate. Subtract the price from 100 to get the implied December mean. Assume the latest available effective rate of 3.88% continues for 1–9 December. Multiply the monthly mean by 31, subtract nine days at 3.88%, then divide by 22 to obtain the implied average from 10 December. Realised rates can move within a target range, and the futures price can contain a premium. Many outcome distributions fit the same average. Changes shown are computed before rounding the displayed levels.

Each calculation uses the preceding published effective-rate observation. CME’s settlement window for the front contracts ends at 2 p.m. Chicago time. The 18 November settlement followed the 2 p.m. ET release of the October FOMC minutes. Weekly jobless claims came out at 8:30 a.m. ET on 19 November, before Jefferson’s remarks. These daily intervals include both policy news and other market information.

Window definitions and data sources

Each pre-event window ends at the last jointly quoted close strictly before the event date. A five-session change compares that close with the fifth earlier quoted close. The spread is the ten-year yield minus the two-year yield. If both yields rise, the curve steepens when the ten-year rises by more. The event-date and following-close rows show changes from the immediately preceding quoted close. A dash marks an unavailable comparison. Weekends, holidays and missing joint observations are skipped when counting sessions.

US Treasury par yields use indicative quotes sampled at approximately 15:30 New York time. Yield levels reflect both expected future short rates and term premia. A change in slope alone cannot separate those contributions. A daily change can include other news. For minute-by-minute speech windows, use timestamped quotes in the event calculator.

What did dealers expect the Fed to do?

Before each scheduled FOMC meeting in 2022–24, New York Fed primary dealers reported their most likely target rate. Many surveys also asked how much probability dealers placed on each possible outcome. The replies predate the decisions. The New York Fed made the aggregates public after the minutes.

Loading the meeting surveys…

Compare all 24 meetings
How the forecasts and errors are measured

The dates are the survey’s distribution and response deadline. The New York Fed published aggregate results after the meeting minutes, so these are retrospective records of answers made before the decision. The tables use the original premeeting panel. The median of each dealer’s most likely midpoint and the average probability assigned to each bin answer different questions. Dealers can agree on a most likely outcome while assigning substantial probability elsewhere.

The signed error is the realised target-range midpoint minus the median modal forecast, in basis points, after rounding the realised midpoint to the survey’s published precision. A positive error means the target was higher than the forecast. Gross errors are compared with the simple forecast of an unchanged target. Probability bins retain the New York Fed’s published rounding and can total slightly more or less than 100%. One basis point equals 0.01 percentage point.

“Move on 25 bp grid” identifies the change from the premeeting midpoint that lands in a given bin, assuming quarter-point steps. The first and last bins may cover several changes. They are shown as tail ranges. A missing meeting distribution means the probability question asked about another horizon.

A dealer can expect substantial easing over the next twelve months while favouring a quarter-point cut at the first meeting. Use the September 2024 probability bins to examine expectations for that specific decision.

The separate speech observation

Event windows and interpretation

The pre-meeting change runs from the fifth to the first jointly quoted Treasury close strictly before the event date, spanning four close-to-close changes. Daily Treasury par yields reflect indicative quotes around 15:30 New York time. USMPD measures the on-the-run two-year yield from 10 minutes before to 20 minutes after the statement. No intervening overnight or pre-release move is added.

The table counts every matched meeting in the selected sample. The directional share and aligned median use meetings with two non-zero moves. Alignment multiplies the statement move by the sign of the earlier move, so a negative value measures movement against the earlier direction. For the 1 bp sensitivity check both the earlier and the statement moves must reach 1 bp in absolute value. The latter condition is only known after the release.

The benchmark preserves the up and down totals on each side within each calendar year and calculates the average agreement across all possible within-year pairings. The leave-one-year-out range recalculates the observed share after omitting each year in turn. These comparisons describe the sample. Yields also reflect term premia and other economic news. Estimating the probability of a particular policy move requires a contract tied to the decision and assumptions about its possible outcomes.

Which history better predicted the size of the next rate move?

A portfolio manager budgeting risk before a Fed statement would have made smaller errors overall using the typical two-year move from 2009–17. Its edge disappeared in 2022–26. At ECB decisions the two historical estimates were only 0.10 bp apart, and neither captured the larger German yield moves in the later years.

Dropping one evaluation year at a time leaves the 2009–17 forecast ahead for the US two-year by 0.24–0.58 bp. The 2000–08 forecast keeps a 0.025–0.043 bp edge for the German two-year. These ranges measure sensitivity to individual years. The meetings within a policy cycle share economic shocks, and the ranges do not quantify sampling uncertainty.

Each quoted announcement gets equal weight. A zero is an observation. One of 96 ECB statements in 2009–17 lacks the German yield pair. US evaluation runs from 31 January 2018 to 28 October 2026, and ECB evaluation from 25 January 2018 to 11 June 2026. Results use the historical files available on 20 November 2026. Cutoffs were chosen retrospectively. Original release-day dataset vintages could differ.

The US window starts ten minutes before the statement and ends twenty minutes after. ECB observations compare median Frankfurt quotes at 13:25–13:35 and 14:00–14:10, shifting to 13:55–14:05 and 14:30–14:40 from July 2022. News released with the statement, the prevailing rate level and changes in meeting frequency can all affect the distribution. Attribution to a chair or a particular policy would require further evidence.

On 18 September 2024 the two-year Treasury fell 8.58 bp in the statement window. The 2000–08 benchmark missed its magnitude by 5.09 bp, against 6.96 bp for 2009–17. Both underestimated risk on a day when the decision and projections arrived together. The direction of that move was unknown to either forecast before the release.

Pre-event pricing and sample construction

Each date contributes once, including dates with several speeches. The medians of the two yields and their spread are calculated separately. The 2s10s spread is the ten-year yield minus the two-year yield. Daily Treasury yields reflect both the expected path of short rates and term premia. Other economic news during the window can affect both. Estimating the probability of a particular policy decision requires an instrument and assumptions about the possible outcomes. The meeting windows above measure a different interval around the announcement itself.

Sample, instruments and window definitions

Eligible dates have a published observation window. A missing quote is an eligible window without the selected instrument. Dates with no such window are counted separately. Zero changes remain in the sample. The median absolute move is the middle observation after sorting by magnitude. The signed median and middle 50% retain direction. Quantiles use linear interpolation, and rankings use absolute changes before display rounding.

Rates and slope changes use basis points. Equity and currency changes use percent. US and German government yields refer to different issuers. EUR/USD is dollars per euro. Price changes can reflect several kinds of news. Each source uses its own trading interval for the selected event type.

Which 2024 Fed meetings moved the two-year yield unusually far?

The target fell 25 basis points on 18 December, yet the Treasury’s daily two-year yield rose 10 basis points. It was the only one of eight scheduled 2024 meetings to cross twice the previous month’s daily volatility. Twenty quoted days later the yield was 8 basis points below its meeting-day level.

How the daily screen is calculated

Use the US Treasury’s two-year par yield to put the move on each FOMC day in context. The screen compares the absolute daily change with twice the sample standard deviation of the 21 preceding quoted-day changes. The meeting day is excluded from the volatility estimate. The final column of figures measures the yield change from the meeting-day quote to the twentieth subsequent quote.

Treasury samples indicative quotations around 3:30 p.m. New York time. Its day-to-day move can include news that arrived hours before the statement. A yield change omits coupon income and duration, so it cannot establish a bond return. One qualifying meeting in a single calendar year is too little evidence to estimate trading performance.
